findings.desc: Verification coverage gap: protected outputDir refusal is asserted in the smoke at packages/main/src/tasks/memory-real-data-benchmark-smoke.ts:205 and :211, but no verificationIntent explicitly owns that behavior. CHK-002 edge intent only covers non-authority boundary labeling, so protected outputDir remains untracked by checklist acceptance criteria even though the evidence note mentions it.

memory_benchmark_real_data is not config-driven for story roots: resolveStoryRootPaths only adds loadConfig(root).storyDir when it starts with ".koala/" (packages/main/src/core/memory-benchmark-real-data.ts:384-392), while buildReasons still hard-fails on missing ".koala/story/actives" (packages/main/src/core/memory-benchmark-real-data.ts:795-802). That conflicts with the project config/default contract where storyDir is configurable and defaults to docs/story/actives (packages/main/src/core/config.ts:269-274), and StoryStore reads the configured path plus legacy fallback (packages/main/src/core/store.ts:35-61). Verified repros: (1) storyDir=".koala/custom-actives" with real activity + index.json => FAIL "missing real story source root: .koala/story/actives"; (2) storyDir="docs/story/actives" with real activity + index.json => collector ignores the configured root and returns the same false FAIL. This breaks host-neutral/boundary correctness because PASS/FAIL depends on repo layout instead of whether real lifecycle data exists.

[HIGH] packages/main/src/core/memory-benchmark-real-data.ts:833-873 allows --outputDir inside .koala/story/actives, so memory_benchmark_real_data can write corpus/gold/query/result files into story-managed state even though packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts marks it readOnly. A temporary-root repro wrote files under .koala/story/actives/B-x/benchmark-artifacts successfully. Fix by rejecting configured storyDir/.koala lifecycle paths in assertAllowedOutputDir or by reclassifying the command as a mutating command with owner/phase gates.

[MEDIUM] packages/main/src/core/memory-benchmark-real-data.ts:364-379 reads activity entries from command/type/success, but the real runtime log format uses tool/detail/status. On the live worktree run, exported raw_event_memory rows rendered as command=unknown and success=n/a for every sample taken from .koala/activity.jsonl, so the “real-data” corpus loses the actual lifecycle command names and outcomes. Fix by parsing tool/detail/status first (with command/type/success as legacy fallbacks) and add a smoke assertion against the current activity log schema.
